posts.title: Researcher draft (ID to be assigned): "Water boils at 100 °C at sea level": approximately; 99.974 °C at standard pressure (ITS-90)

sources.finding: Standard pressure1013.25hPa/mb;100–1050mb is described as meteorological usage range. It does not establish an empirical sea-level weather interval. Author's reported direct403 is their retrieval history; reviewer could read through browser.

Historical fixed-point assignments include100 C for water in ITS-27; IPTS-68 allowed tin as alternative to steam point. Triple point replaced ice-point unit/calibration roles earlier than1990. ITS-90 took effect1January1990 and uses specified practical calibration/interpolation.
sources.limits: State specific scales and their assignments. Do not imply the modern Celsius/SI unit itself was defined by a0/100 two-point water definition until1990, or that water physically changed. Full original scale specifications and all historical realizations not audited.

sources.locator: R6-95(2018), cover; printed2 notation note; printed5 saturation treatment
sources.finding: Formulation uses ITS-90 temperatures, explicitly unaffected by2019 SI revision; saturation computed by phase-equilibrium equations. This is reference-model content fitted to data, not a new measurement.
sources.limits: No independent IAPWS95 implementation or uncertainty propagation performed. Shared model dependence with the NIST implementation reported by author must be preserved; NIST-specific equation selection not independently read due numeric endpoint failure.

sources.finding: Compilation gives373.17 ±0.04 K, average of7values. Subtracting273.15 gives100.02 ±0.04 C, NOT99.98 ±0.04 C as draft says. Reference99.974 C is0.046 K below that mean, just outside the simple printed±0.04 interval.
sources.limits: Uncertainty convention, constituent values/scales and independent source provenance not examined. Do not claim conflict or agreement at a specified confidence level; delete the draft's arithmetic/within-stated-uncertainty consistency claim.

findings.text: Correct373.17 K conversion:100.02 C.99.98 C is an arithmetic error.99.974 C is outside the literal373.13–373.21 K interval, so the stated within-uncertainty claim is not justified. Do not promote this to statistically significant disagreement without examining uncertainty conventions and original data.

findings.target: interpolations in latest WMO and Penn State supplements
findings.text: Independent arithmetic reproduces listed six rounded results from supplied endpoints. Original NIST grid and99.9743 output inaccessible; computations remain conditional on supplied rows. One standard-pressure residual does not bound interpolation elsewhere; no general error bound or two-decimal physical accuracy accepted.

Use rounded IAPWS99.974 C with ITS-90/ordinary pure-water saturation/101.325kPa scope. Preserve approximate wording and practical-versus-thermodynamic scale distinction. Specific historical scale assignments are supported; universal earlier-scale generalizations and modern unit-definition timeline are not.

May retain attributed educational guideline separately, with lack of sampling methodology. Do not state most local sea-level water boils99.0–100.7 C. A hypothetical mapping of specified ACTUAL pressures may be labelled a conditional calculation; no physical distribution inferred.
